name: Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport
before:
The main gateway to Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang province and one of the big names in the Yangtze River Delta. The airport sits on the southern shore of the Qiantang River in Xiaoshan District, around 27km east of the city centre, which means a straightforward run into town by metro, direct airport bus or the elevated expressway built above the existing highway.

It is a genuinely large operation. In 2025 it handled just over 50 million passengers, making it the seventh busiest in China, and it moved close to 800,000 tonnes of cargo. Air China, China Eastern, China Southern, Hainan Airlines and Xiamen Airlines all treat it as a focus city, so domestic connections across China are plentiful.

There are four terminals. Terminals 1 and 3 handle domestic flights only, Terminal 2 takes international and regional services, and Terminal 4, which opened in September 2022, handles a mix of both. The buildings were designed by architecture firm Aedas.

International routes lean heavily towards East and Southeast Asia, with further connections to Europe, South Asia, Africa and Oceania.
after:
The main airport for Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang province and one of the big names in the Yangtze River Delta. From its site around 27km east of the city centre, it is a straightforward run into town by metro or airport bus.

It is a genuinely large operation. In 2025 it handled just over 50 million passengers, making it the seventh busiest in China. It also moved close to 800,000 tonnes of cargo. Air China, China Eastern, China Southern, Hainan Airlines and Xiamen Airlines all fly from here, so domestic connections across China are plentiful.

Terminal 4, which opened in September 2022, takes international and regional flights and some domestic ones, while Terminals 1 and 3 handle domestic flights only. Check which terminal a domestic flight uses.

claims.wasBefore: on the southern shore of the Qiantang River in Xiaoshan District
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator says only that it is in the east of Hangzhou, 27 km from the centre, and OurAirports places it in Hangzhou without a district.

claims.wasBefore: by metro, direct airport bus or the elevated expressway built above the existing highway
claims.why: The expressway rests on Wikipedia alone, and the city bus makes stops on the way (operator, Wikipedia), so 'direct' goes. Metro and airport bus are kept (see above).

claims.wasBefore: all treat it as a focus city
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for 'focus city'; softened to the airlines flying from here (see above).

claims.claim: There are four terminals
claims.why: The count is not settled for today: the operator's capability page counts three domestic terminals and one international, but what Terminal 2 does since the international flights left it in April 2023 is not stated anywhere readable, and the operator's transfer guide names only Terminals 3 and 4. The text names the terminals in use instead.

claims.claim: Terminal 2 takes international and regional services
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2 takes international and regional services
claims.why: Out of date since 7 April 2023, when the operator moved all international and regional flights from Terminal 2 to Terminal 4 (the operator's own timeline). Wikipedia's sentence is stale.

claims.claim: Terminal 4 handles a mix of both
claims.why: Made specific: Terminal 4 takes all the international and regional flights and some domestic ones (see above).

claims.claim: the buildings were designed by Aedas
claims.wasBefore: The buildings were designed by architecture firm Aedas.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone: Aedas's old project page (www1.aedas.com) did not connect, the page at its current site answered 404, and the archived copy Wikipedia cites is in the web archive, which the network policy blocks. 'The buildings' would also take in Terminal 4, whose designer no source here names.

claims.claim: international routes lean towards East and Southeast Asia, with further links to Europe, South Asia, Africa and Oceania
claims.wasBefore: International routes lean heavily towards East and Southeast Asia, with further connections to Europe, South Asia, Africa and Oceania.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator gives only counts (53 international and regional destinations at the end of 2024), its new-routes page is mostly 2008 to 2016, and its September 2026 summer report names only Asian routes (a new Busan service, more flights to Ho Chi Minh City and Kuala Lumpur). Nothing current describes the whole international network.

opinion.text: It is a genuinely large operation.
opinion.why: The old text's judgement, kept: seventh busiest in China with just over 50 million passengers in 2025 (CAAC).

opinion.text: Check which terminal a domestic flight uses.
opinion.why: Advice on the confirmed split: the operator's transfer guide sends Air China, China Southern and Sichuan Airlines domestic flights to Terminal 4 and other airlines' to Terminal 3.
